message.content:
Here are some of the major airports in the United States, ranked by passenger traffic and importance:

| Airport (IATA) | City / State | Passenger Traffic (2022) | Notes |
|----------------|--------------|--------------------------|-------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International (ATL)** | Atlanta, GA | ~107 million | Largest by passengers; major hub for Delta Air Lines. |
| **Los Angeles International (LAX)** | Los Angeles, CA | ~88 million | Major West Coast hub; key for international flights to Asia & Latin America. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International (ORD)** | Chicago, IL | ~84 million | One of the busiest airports worldwide; hub for United & American Airlines. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International (DFW)** | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | ~70 million | Hub for American Airlines; one of the largest single-runway airports. |
| **Denver International (DEN)** | Denver, CO | ~63 million | Hub for United & Southwest; largest airport by land area in the U.S. |
| **John F. Kennedy International (JFK)** | New York, NY | ~61 million | Major hub for American & Delta; primary gateway to Europe. |
| **San Francisco International (SFO)** | San Francisco, CA | ~58 million | Hub for United & Alaska Airlines; key for transpacific routes. |
| **Seattle‑Tacoma International (SEA)** | Seattle, WA | ~55 million | Hub for Alaska Airlines & Delta; growing hub for tech‑industry travel. |
| **McCarran International (LAS)** | Las Vegas, NV | ~54 million | Hub for Southwest & United; major leisure destination. |
| **Orlando International (MCO)** | Orlando, FL | ~53 million | Hub for JetBlue & Southwest; major tourist gateway. |

These airports serve as major hubs for domestic and international travel, host numerous airlines, and handle tens of millions of passengers each year.
